claims.text: The fare ledger for this trip records airport_surcharge of SGD 0.00 and a charged total of SGD 27.90 that is exactly the quoted fare, so the platform raised no airport surcharge on this trip at all. The SGD 40 the driver took by PayNow therefore corresponds to no line of the fare_breakdown: it is an off-ledger charge for a line the platform never billed, and the rider's own reading of the bill ('no surcharge, the quoted price') is confirmed by the ledger.

The driver's own in-app message reads 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider's reply is 'ok sent'. The record thus shows the driver demanding and receiving an off-app SGD 40 payment for a surcharge that appears nowhere on the ledger — a demand, not an offer the rider freely chose, and one that preceded the payment. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a line the ledger does not bear is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that limb is expressly available whether or not any deviation exists.

The Changi airport surcharge is a platform line defined and itemised by this policy's own fare model (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak, on a trip ORIGINATING at Changi) — it is not a cost 'the app doesn't cover', and even at its highest it is a fraction of the SGD 40 collected. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, and POL-RD-11 permits nothing to be charged beyond the quote except ERP and tolls actually crossed, a properly chargeable airport surcharge, and the waiting-time fee, each of which must be itemised on the fare_breakdown. An SGD 40 private PayNow collection for a line the ledger shows at 0.00 is none of those.

No distance- or time-based justification exists for any extra charge. The driver's own trace measures 15.79 km against an optimal 15.5 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% — below both POL-RD-01 establishment tests of 20% and 0.8 km, and the derived status is 'no deviation'. The rider was driven the quoted route, so the SGD 40 purchased no distance, no time and no detour; it is money for nothing.

No traffic advisory covers this trip's corridor or window. EV-ADVIS-00531-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the driver cannot invoke a road closure under POL-RD-03, and the absence itself is citable under POL-GEN-02. Nothing external to the trip explains or excuses a private SGD 40 demand.

Failing a refund under POL-RD-09(4): the sum the rider actually lost — the SGD 40 — appears on no artifact in this bundle at all, not on the fare_breakdown (airport_surcharge 0.00), not in the gps_trace, and not in the trip_record. A disputed sum the record cannot carry to the platform's 0.70 confidence floor engages the escalation rule in POL-RD-10; on that footing no monetary ruling should issue on this record and the matter should be held for a human reviewer rather than left with the driver.

Both establishment tests fail: the excess is neither greater than the 0.8 km absolute gate nor greater than 20% of the optimal distance. No route deviation exists, and POL-RD-01 directs that the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test; the trace already fails both gates at 1.87%. For completeness, even on the trip_record's rounded 15.8 km the excess over the 15.5 km optimal is 0.3 km — still far below the 0.8 km and 20% gates. No reading of the distance fields carries the rider's deviation claim.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. This trace is COMPLETE with 100% coverage, no gaps and a 10 s cadence, and it shows only 1.87% excess. The burden is never discharged, and the driver is not put to invoking any exculpatory clause at all.

The fare is an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the quoted fare of SGD 27.90 equals the charged total of SGD 27.90, with charged_over_quote of 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, no distance-or-time refund is available however large any excess, and the rider's only monetary remedies — the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote, and a pass-through correction — both come to nothing here.

The ledger carries no ERP gantries and tolls_erp of 0.00, and the airport_surcharge line is 0.00. There is no charge line that the gps_trace fails to match, so the standalone billing-integrity remedy in POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged on this record.

This trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge is in principle a properly chargeable item for this trip under the fare model. POL-RD-09(4) confines a billing-integrity finding to an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport, which this trip is not; the rider's premise that any airport-pickup surcharge is illegitimate has no support in the loaded policy.

The SGD 40 the rider says she sent by PayNow appears nowhere in the fare_breakdown; it is an off-platform transfer between the parties, not a fare line item. The route-deviation clauses compute refunds only against fare_breakdown lines (POL-RD-09, POL-RD-11), and POL-GEN-03 moves money only as a fare refund to the filing party or a driver payment. The chat log shows the driver asked and the rider replied 'ok sent', and the counterparty statement records the payment as voluntary. Even taking the rider's account at its highest, no clause in the loaded policy licenses an order against the driver to return an off-platform payment, so nothing is refundable in this forum.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both of you, and I want to be straight about what this forum can and cannot do.

THE FARE (SGD 27.90). This was an upfront-quoted trip (RYDE_X, EV-FARE-00531). The quoted fare was SGD 27.90 and the amount charged on the platform was SGD 27.90, so charged_over_quote is 0.00 — nothing was added over the quote. The only other possible lines are the airport surcharge, recorded at SGD 0.00, and ERP/tolls, recorded at SGD 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges are fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available on an upfront-quoted trip, and there is no pass-through line to correct. The platform charge of SGD 27.90 is correct and stands.

THE ROUTE. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531), which recorded 15.79 km against an optimal route of 15.50 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%. That fails both POL-RD-01 tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%). The trace is complete (100% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps), so it is not impaired and no corroboration is needed. The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00531-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore carries nothing, and no closure exoneration arises. No route deviation is established.

THE SGD 40. Ms Rider, the SGD 40 you describe is not ignored — it is recorded in the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00531): the driver wrote 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' at 22:49:40 and you replied 'ok sent' at 22:50:40, and the driver's statement confirms he asked and was paid. So the payment is documented and I do not doubt you made it. The difficulty is remedy. The SGD 40 is not a line of the fare breakdown, and this tribunal's refund machinery runs only on fare-breakdown lines. POL-RD-09(4) refunds a charge line for a gantry the trace never crossed, or an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport. This trip DID originate at Changi Terminal 2 (EV-TRIP-00531), and the ledger's surcharge line is SGD 0.00, so there is no wrongly applied surcharge line to refund — the SGD 40 was never a platform charge. No other clause in the loaded policy reaches a private transfer between the two of you, and POL-GEN-03 lets money move only as a fare refund or a platform payment to the driver. So the SGD 40 cannot be ordered returned in this forum, and I have not manufactured a referral to do it: a referral exists only where a clause produces one, and none does here (POL-RD-06(c) requires a material deviation and an established pattern, neither of which exists; POL-RD-09(4) requires a billing-integrity defect on the ledger, which does not exist).

ON ESCALATION. POL-RD-10 escalates only on its listed grounds. None is present: confidence is above 0.70; all identifiers match TRP-00531; the trace is unimpaired; the timestamps agree (started 22:51:40, ended 23:13:40 on both trip record and trace); no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; any refund is zero, not above SGD 150 or the charged total; the evidence is consistent rather than two-sidedly contradictory; and every fare line has a counterpart. So this is not an escalation case, and the disputed sum is not held.

WHAT I CAN SAY PLAINLY. The driver's in-app message that the airport surcharge 'cannot' go through the app does not match this platform's fare model, under which the airport surcharge is a platform line (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak on a trip originating at Changi) and the platform charged none on this trip. The SGD 40 was collected off-platform and is outside what this fare-dispute process can order returned; if you wish to pursue it, that is a matter for the platform's trust-and-safety channel or between the two of you. On the money in this case, the outcome is NO_ACTION: the SGD 27.90 platform charge stands as charged and correct, and no refund or driver compensation issues.

To the rider: the fare you were charged was correct and no route-deviation refund is due. To the driver: the fare stands, but the off-app SGD 40 is not something this policy can order returned either.

ROUTE DEVIATION. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531, weight 1.0), which records 15.79 km against the 15.5 km optimal route — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%, below both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%). Even on the trip_record's rounded 15.8 km the excess is 0.3 km. Both advocates agree, and the record confirms, that no deviation exists, so POL-RD-02 and the distance refund it computes do not run, and POL-RD-08's burden is never discharged.

FARE. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (EV-FARE-00531, weight 1.0). The quoted fare of SGD 27.90 equals the charged total of SGD 27.90 (charged_over_quote 0.00), so under POL-RD-11 there is no amount by which the charge exceeds the quote and no distance-or-time refund is available.

PASS-THROUGH / BILLING INTEGRITY. The ledger carries no ERP gantries (tolls_erp 0.00) and its airport_surcharge line is 0.00. There is therefore no charge line for POL-RD-09(4) to correct. I reject the rider's submission that POL-RD-09(4) fires: that limb addresses a charge line the ledger wrongly bears, and here the ledger bears no surcharge line at all. I also note the trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so a Changi surcharge would be a properly chargeable line under the fare model (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak) rather than the billing defect the rider's premise assumes; the driver's claim that the surcharge 'cannot [go] in app' is not borne out by the policy.

THE SGD 40. This sum appears on no artifact in the bundle and on no line of the fare_breakdown. The money remedies this policy gives are fare refunds traceable to a fare_breakdown line (POL-RD-02, POL-RD-09, POL-RD-11) or a driver payment, and POL-GEN-03 permits nothing else. There is no fare line to refund and no clause that orders the return of a private off-platform PayNow transfer, so I cannot order the SGD 40 returned here. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00531, weight 1.0) does record the driver writing 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider replying 'ok sent', and SGD 40 is far above any surcharge the fare model defines — a conduct concern, but not one this route-deviation policy turns into a refund or a referral on this record.

ESCALATION. I reject the rider's submission that POL-RD-10 requires escalation. None of its triggers fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is whole (100% coverage, 133 fixes, 10-second cadence, no gaps); no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing or field-less artifact; no charge line is unmatched. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00531-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is citable as an absence, but no closure was invoked and it changes nothing.

RESULT. The present state stands: the SGD 27.90 charge is not refunded, no driver compensation is due, and no referral is produced. The open question of the driver's off-app SGD 40 request is not one this policy decides; if the rider wishes to pursue it, it belongs with the platform's conduct team through in-app support.

To both parties.

This dispute is about the SGD 40 the rider paid the driver by PayNow for an 'airport surcharge' that does not appear on the trip's bill. The platform fare for the trip is correct, and no clause in this policy reaches the off-platform payment, so no refund issues.

1) The bill. This was an upfront-quoted trip. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00531) records a quoted fare of SGD 27.90 and a charged total of SGD 27.90 — the rider was charged exactly the price quoted at booking (charged_over_quote 0.00). Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available; there is no amount by which the charge exceeded the quote, so no excess-over-quote refund arises either.

2) No route deviation. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531, weight 1.0), which records 15.79 km against a 15.5 km optimal route: an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal) fail. No deviation is established, so POL-RD-02 does not run and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause. The rider is right that she was driven the quoted route.

3) No billing-integrity defect. The breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines (ERP 0.00) and an airport_surcharge line of SGD 0.00. The trip originated at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge would in any event be a properly chargeable line under the fare model; POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity limb is confined to a gantry line the trace never passes, or an airport surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport. Neither is present, so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged and no billing-integrity referral arises.

4) The SGD 40. The payment is established as a fact, not a gap in the record: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00531, weight 1.0) records the driver's message 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider's reply 'ok sent', and the driver's own counter-statement confirms 'she paid'. The rider's submission that the SGD 40 appears on no artifact is therefore not accepted. But the payment is an off-platform transfer between the parties: it corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown. The route-deviation money clauses (POL-RD-09, POL-RD-11) recompute or correct fare-breakdown lines, and POL-GEN-03 moves money only as a fare refund or a driver payment computed from those clauses. No clause in this policy licenses an order that the driver return an off-platform payment, so the SGD 40 cannot be refunded here. A driver's claim to a Changi surcharge on an airport-originating trip is at most the fare model's SGD 6.00/SGD 8.00 item, and that line was billed at 0.00; a private collection above it is a payment-integrity matter outside the route-deviation rules, which the rider may raise through the appropriate channel.

5) No escalation. The rider asks for POL-RD-10 escalation, but no trigger fires: trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is complete and unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s cadence); timestamps are consistent; no exculpatory clause has been invoked against an absent artifact; and no refund is computed, so the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling cannot be exceeded. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00531-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, as the rider correctly disclosed); a missing artifact carries no fact, and its absence matters only if a closure is asserted, which it is not, so it changes nothing.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the charged fare of SGD 27.90 is left in place (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), with no refund and no driver compensation.

The payment is established as a fact, not a gap in the record: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00531, weight 1.0) records the driver's message 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider's reply 'ok sent', and the driver's own counter-statement confirms 'she paid'. The rider's submission that the SGD 40 appears on no artifact is therefore not accepted. But the payment is an off-platform transfer between the parties: it corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown. The route-deviation money clauses (POL-RD-09, POL-RD-11) recompute or correct fare-breakdown lines, and POL-GEN-03 moves money only as a fare refund or a driver payment computed from those clauses. No clause in this policy licenses an order that the driver return an off-platform payment, so the SGD 40 cannot be refunded here. A driver's claim to a Changi surcharge on an airport-originating trip is at most the fare model's SGD 6.00/SGD 8.00 item, and that line was billed at 0.00; a private collection above it is a payment-integrity matter outside the route-deviation rules, which the rider may raise through the appropriate channel.

5) No escalation. The rider asks for POL-RD-10 escalation, but no trigger fires: trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is complete and unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s cadence); timestamps are consistent; no exculpatory clause has been invoked against an absent artifact; and no refund is computed, so the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling cannot be exceeded. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00531-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, as the rider correctly disclosed); a missing artifact carries no fact, and its absence matters only if a closure is asserted, which it is not, so it changes nothing.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the charged fare of SGD 27.90 is left in place (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), with no refund and no driver compensation."},"discarded_claims":[]}

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this ruling deals with two separate things — the SGD 27.90 the platform charged for TRP-00531, and the separate SGD 40 the driver collected by PayNow.

THE FARE AND THE ROUTE ARE CLEAN. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00531, weight 1.0) is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the quoted fare of SGD 27.90 equals the charged total of SGD 27.90, so charged_over_quote is SGD 0.00. The airport_surcharge line is SGD 0.00, tolls_erp is SGD 0.00 and there are no ERP gantries. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00531, weight 1.0) records 15.79 km driven against a 15.5 km optimal route — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% — below both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%). The rider's own claim that no distance was bought is correct: no route deviation exists, so POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION, and because the fare is upfront-quoted POL-RD-11 also closes the distance-and-time refund route (the charged total is not above the quote plus any properly chargeable pass-through). The rider's and driver's distance claims are accepted and agree.

THE SGD 40. The record does support the rider's account of what happened: the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00531, weight 1.0) shows the driver writing 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider replying 'ok sent', and the driver's own counterparty statement confirms he asked for and received a payment. The rider is also right that the driver's premise was false: this policy's fare model makes the Changi airport surcharge a platform line (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak) on a trip originating at Changi, not a cost 'the app doesn't cover'. But I cannot order the SGD 40 returned. The rider's POL-RD-09(4) argument is rejected: that limb reaches only (a) a charge line for a gantry the GPS trace never passes, or (b) an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport. There are no gantry lines here, and this trip does originate at Changi Terminal 2, so a surcharge would be properly chargeable — and in any event the ledger carries no surcharge line at all. The SGD 40 is not a fare_breakdown line; it is a private transfer between the parties, and POL-RD-09 corrects fare lines, not off-platform payments. POL-RD-11, POL-RD-09 and POL-GEN-03 move money only as a fare refund to the filing party, a pass-through correction, or a platform/fee-funded payment to the driver. No clause in the loaded policy licenses an order to return an off-platform payment, so nothing is refundable on this record and no compensation is due to the driver either (there is no unbilled distance — the billed 15.8 km is not short of the trace).

THE ESCALATION ARGUMENT (rider) is rejected. POL-RD-10 lists its triggers and none fires: trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (trigger 2 no); the trace is COMPLETE at 100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s cadence, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (trigger 3 no); timestamps are consistent (trigger 4 no); no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact — the driver never asserted a closure, a rider-requested detour or a relocation (trigger 5 no); the refund does not approach the ceilings (trigger 6 no); there is no comparably strong contradictory evidence (trigger 7 no); every fare line has a counterpart (trigger 8 no); and confidence is above the 0.70 floor (trigger 1 no). Nor is the SGD 40 'a sum the record cannot carry' — the chat log and the driver's statement carry it. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00531-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is noted, but the driver invoked no road-closure excuse, so its absence decides nothing and it carries no finding.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the fare ledger, the GPS trace and the chat log — is at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the bundle mean is context only. Confidence is set at 0.90.

OUTCOME. No clause provides a monetary remedy, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. The SGD 27.90 charge stands as charged, and no refund or driver compensation issues. The SGD 40 is an off-platform payment outside this forum; nothing in this ruling prevents the rider from raising the driver's off-app surcharge demand with the platform's off-platform-payment or fraud process, and that remains the proper route for it.

ledger.claim: The fare ledger for this trip records airport_surcharge of SGD 0.00 and a charged total of SGD 27.90 that is exactly the quoted fare, so the platform raised no airport surcharge on this trip at all. The SGD 40 the driver took by PayNow therefore corresponds to no line of the fare_breakdown: it is an off-ledger charge for a line the platform never billed, and the rider's own reading of the bill ('no surcharge, the quoted price') is confirmed by the ledger.

The driver's own in-app message reads 'airport surcharge cannot in app, paynow 40 pls' and the rider's reply is 'ok sent'. The record thus shows the driver demanding and receiving an off-app SGD 40 payment for a surcharge that appears nowhere on the ledger — a demand, not an offer the rider freely chose, and one that preceded the payment. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a line the ledger does not bear is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that limb is expressly available whether or not any deviation exists.

The Changi airport surcharge is a platform line defined and itemised by this policy's own fare model (SGD 6.00 off-peak / SGD 8.00 peak, on a trip ORIGINATING at Changi) — it is not a cost 'the app doesn't cover', and even at its highest it is a fraction of the SGD 40 collected. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, and POL-RD-11 permits nothing to be charged beyond the quote except ERP and tolls actually crossed, a properly chargeable airport surcharge, and the waiting-time fee, each of which must be itemised on the fare_breakdown. An SGD 40 private PayNow collection for a line the ledger shows at 0.00 is none of those.

No distance- or time-based justification exists for any extra charge. The driver's own trace measures 15.79 km against an optimal 15.5 km — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87% — below both POL-RD-01 establishment tests of 20% and 0.8 km, and the derived status is 'no deviation'. The rider was driven the quoted route, so the SGD 40 purchased no distance, no time and no detour; it is money for nothing.

No traffic advisory covers this trip's corridor or window. EV-ADVIS-00531-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the driver cannot invoke a road closure under POL-RD-03, and the absence itself is citable under POL-GEN-02. Nothing external to the trip explains or excuses a private SGD 40 demand.

Failing a refund under POL-RD-09(4): the sum the rider actually lost — the SGD 40 — appears on no artifact in this bundle at all, not on the fare_breakdown (airport_surcharge 0.00), not in the gps_trace, and not in the trip_record. A disputed sum the record cannot carry to the platform's 0.70 confidence floor engages the escalation rule in POL-RD-10; on that footing no monetary ruling should issue on this record and the matter should be held for a human reviewer rather than left with the driver.

The governing distance measurement under POL-RD-01 is the gps_trace, and it records 15.79 km driven against a 15.5 km optimal route — an excess of 0.29 km, or 1.87%. Both establishment tests fail: the excess is neither greater than the 0.8 km absolute gate nor greater than 20% of the optimal distance. No route deviation exists, and POL-RD-01 directs that the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test; the trace already fails both gates at 1.87%. For completeness, even on the trip_record's rounded 15.8 km the excess over the 15.5 km optimal is 0.3 km — still far below the 0.8 km and 20% gates. No reading of the distance fields carries the rider's deviation claim.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. This trace is COMPLETE with 100% coverage, no gaps and a 10 s cadence, and it shows only 1.87% excess. The burden is never discharged, and the driver is not put to invoking any exculpatory clause at all.

The fare is an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the quoted fare of SGD 27.90 equals the charged total of SGD 27.90, with charged_over_quote of 0.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, no distance-or-time refund is available however large any excess, and the rider's only monetary remedies — the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote, and a pass-through correction — both come to nothing here.

The ledger carries no ERP gantries and tolls_erp of 0.00, and the airport_surcharge line is 0.00. There is no charge line that the gps_trace fails to match, so the standalone billing-integrity remedy in POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged on this record.

This trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 2, so an airport surcharge is in principle a properly chargeable item for this trip under the fare model. POL-RD-09(4) confines a billing-integrity finding to an airport surcharge on a trip that does NOT originate at an airport, which this trip is not; the rider's premise that any airport-pickup surcharge is illegitimate has no support in the loaded policy.

The SGD 40 the rider says she sent by PayNow appears nowhere in the fare_breakdown; it is an off-platform transfer between the parties, not a fare line item. The route-deviation clauses compute refunds only against fare_breakdown lines (POL-RD-09, POL-RD-11), and POL-GEN-03 moves money only as a fare refund to the filing party or a driver payment. The chat log shows the driver asked and the rider replied 'ok sent', and the counterparty statement records the payment as voluntary. Even taking the rider's account at its highest, no clause in the loaded policy licenses an order against the driver to return an off-platform payment, so nothing is refundable in this forum.
